fields.meta_description: Build a CRM landing page whose leads reach your CRM with their campaign, owner and history attached, and keep a copy. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build a CRM Landing Page Whose Leads Arrive Ready to Work
fields.hero_description: Get a CRM landing page that sends each lead to your CRM with its campaign and owner, plus a copy in a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What a CRM Landing Page Needs Behind It
fields.features_subheading: A CRM landing page is judged by the record it leaves in your CRM, not by the hero shot. These six parts decide what sales finds there.
fields.feature_1:
Describe the page and the record it creates

Tell Emergent who the page is for and how each new contact should look in your CRM. It builds the page and the table behind it, then changes either one each time you prompt again.
fields.feature_2:
Form fields land in the right CRM properties

Connect HubSpot or any CRM with an API, and each answer syncs into the property you name, such as company size or budget. Sales opens a complete contact, not a pasted note.
fields.feature_3:
The campaign travels with the lead

Ask Emergent to read the campaign name from the link a visitor clicked and store it with the lead. Your CRM can then report which ad brought in each contact, with no hand tagging.
fields.feature_4:
Leads worth a call reach a person

Set a rule on any answer, such as a stated budget over $20,000, and the app sends a Slack, email or in-app alert to the rep who owns it. Anything below the rule waits in the CRM.
fields.feature_5:
A copy of every lead stays yours

Each submission also saves as a row in a database you own, with one column per answer. If you switch CRMs next year, your full lead history moves with you as a sortable table.
fields.feature_6:
Your domain now, your code later

Publish on the domain your ads point to; custom domains are included and use credits. Paid plans export the full code to your GitHub repository. Building is free to start.

fields.usecase_heading: CRM Landing Page Examples by Record
fields.tab_content_1:
The campaign name rides along into HubSpot

Tallowfield Solar installs panels on commercial roofs, and its quote page picks up the campaign tag in the URL a visitor arrives on. Rusk Hollow Bakery's lead reached HubSpot tagged fall-rebate, one of 42 leads that campaign brought in this month.
fields.tab_content_2:
Teo Lindqvist gets every lead from ZIP codes starting 802

Brackwater Insurance splits new business by territory. A lead whose ZIP code starts with 802 is assigned to agent Teo Lindqvist in the CRM, and he gets a Slack direct message. Calla Brennick entered ZIP 80204, and her request arrived under his name.
fields.tab_content_3:
When Dana Okafor writes in again, her record grows

Kestrel Freight hears from the same shippers again and again. Its page looks up each email in the CRM before saving. Dana Okafor already had a record, and her new request for 12 pallets was added to that record instead of starting a second contact.
fields.tab_content_4:
Fernly shows the $76 monthly price before any trial

Fernly sells a CRM to wedding planners, and its own landing page asks how many planners a team has, then multiplies by $19 a seat. Juniper Lane Events entered 4 planners, saw $76 a month, and started a trial saved with that team size.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a CRM Landing Page
fields.howto_description: Follow seven steps to create a CRM landing page whose leads reach the right rep with every field sales needs already filled in.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 List what sales reads before a first call
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Match each field to a CRM property
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Tag every link you send to the page
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Describe the page in a prompt
fields.howto_step_1_des: Ask the rep who makes first calls which three or four facts decide whether a call happens, such as headcount or a start date. Those facts become the form, and anything sales never reads stays off the page.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Open your CRM and find the property each answer should fill. Create any that are missing before you build, and note which ones are dropdowns. The form should offer the same choices the CRM accepts.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Add the utm_campaign parameter to each ad and email link that points at the page, with one exact name per campaign. Google's Analytics help says these parameters let you view which campaigns refer traffic.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Name the offer, each field, the CRM property it fills, and what should happen after a submission. Emergent builds the page from that prompt. Check the first draft against your list from step 01 and prompt again where it drifts.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Write the rule that assigns each submission, by ZIP code or deal size, and name the rep for each branch. Say in the prompt whether that rep should get a Slack message or an email when one arrives.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Send a test lead down every path
fields.howto_step_6_des: Submit one test per routing branch, plus one from an email already in the CRM. Open each record and confirm the campaign and owner arrived, with every property in the right place, before real traffic does.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Publish and sort leads by campaign
fields.howto_step_7_des: Connect your domain and publish. After a week, group the new CRM contacts by campaign and look for the one that sends leads sales never calls back. Fix that ad or the form fields it brings in, by prompt.

faq_plan.q: What is a CRM landing page?
faq_plan.a: A CRM landing page is a single-purpose page whose form sends each visitor's details straight into a CRM as a new contact or lead. The term also covers the page a CRM software company uses to sell its own product. Either way, judge the page by the record it leaves behind: the right fields, the campaign that sent the visitor, and an owner.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a CRM landing page?
faq_plan.a: Decide which CRM properties sales needs, keep the form to those fields, and connect the page to your CRM so every submission becomes a contact. With Emergent's AI landing page builder, you describe the page and the CRM property each field fills in one prompt, and Emergent builds it. Send a test lead before you publish and open the record it created.

faq_plan.q: What fields should a CRM landing page form ask for?
faq_plan.a: Ask only for what decides whether sales calls back, plus an email the CRM can use to match the person to a record. For a B2B quote, that might be company name, team size and timeline. Cut every field a rep does not read before the first call. Whatever the form does collect also saves to a database you own, and stays there if you later drop that property from the CRM.

faq_plan.q: What should a CRM landing page for a software product show?
faq_plan.a: Show the product doing the job buyers came for, such as a new lead landing in a pipeline, then one clear next step. A page selling CRM software is a kind of saas landing page and follows the same discipline: one action, a headline that names the result, and screenshots of believable records. Put the integrations buyers ask about, such as email and calendar, close to the button.

faq_plan.q: How do leads from a CRM landing page get into the CRM?
faq_plan.a: Through the CRM's API: when a visitor submits the form, the page sends the answers to the CRM, and the CRM saves them as a contact or lead. Each form field should map to a named property, or the answers arrive as one block of text. An app built on Emergent connects to any tool with an API and syncs each lead into the properties you choose.

faq_plan.q: How do I track which campaign a CRM landing page lead came from?
faq_plan.a: Read the utm_campaign value from the link the visitor arrived on and save it as a property on the CRM contact. Analytics shows which campaign brought the visit; the CRM property shows which one brought the customer when the deal closes. Pick one spelling per campaign, since a report that groups by exact value counts fall_rebate and fall-rebate as two.

faq_plan.q: How should a CRM landing page decide which rep gets a lead?
faq_plan.a: Route on one answer the form already collects, such as territory or deal size, and name one owner for each value. A law firm landing page, for example, can route each new inquiry by practice area to the attorney who handles that work. Keep a fallback owner for leads that match no rule; without one, they sit unassigned in the CRM.

faq_plan.q: What happens when someone fills out a CRM landing page twice?
faq_plan.a: That depends on the CRM and on how the page writes to it, and the safer course is to set the rule yourself. Either look up the email first and add the new request to the existing record, or create a fresh contact each time. Emergent builds whichever rule you describe in the prompt. Before launch, submit the form twice with one email and open the record.

faq_plan.q: Should a CRM landing page link to the rest of my website?
faq_plan.a: No. Keep the page to one action with no site menu, and let every link on it point at the form. Put a link to your privacy policy beside the email field, because the visitor is handing over contact details. Case studies and product tours belong in the follow-up email, once the lead is already in the CRM and a rep owns it.

faq_plan.q: Should a CRM landing page use animation to show the software?
faq_plan.a: Yes, if the motion explains the product, such as a lead card sliding from the form into a pipeline column. An animated landing page earns its motion when the movement teaches something; animation that only decorates the hero competes with the form for attention. Keep the form itself still, and give the moving piece a plain caption so it still reads with motion turned off.

plan.angle: The top 10 splits two ways: galleries of CRM software marketing pages (Dribbble, SaaSFrame, Saaspo, Figma, Pinterest) that stop at the screenshot, and CRM vendors' own page builders (HubSpot, Vtiger) that only feed their own CRM; the Reddit thread asks how to get page leads into a CRM at all. This page wins by judging a CRM landing page on what each submission writes into the CRM: the campaign it came from, the owner it goes to, the existing record it joins, and, for a CRM company's own page, the trial it starts. Four tabs show those four records; the FAQ answers both meanings of the term, field choice, sync, source tracking, routing, repeat submissions and page design. SaaS, demo and free trial pages are siblings and stay out of the headings; CRM workflow automation belongs to /ai-automation-builder/crm-automation and stays out (no pipeline stages, no follow-up sequences).
